aw.name: New hire
aw.desc: What each level is, why it matters, and your part in protecting quality.

pr.name: Field engineer
pr.desc: Run inspections, verify checklists, log issues, and hit every notice window.

ad.name: QA/QC & Cx admin
ad.desc: Own the plan, the systems of record, the gates and the closeout evidence.

modules.title: QA/QC Foundations
modules.summary: Every inspection on the CDR Campus traces to a four-tier standards stack. Learn who owns quality, where it is recorded, and what happens when work fails.

role.aw: Know who owns quality on your scope and where problems get logged. If you are unsure, stop and ask before proceeding.
role.pr: Verify trade QC, log deficiencies and NCRs in Procore with closure evidence, and escalate repeat failures.
role.ad: Own the QA/QC Plan, NCR trend reporting, and routing between Procore, CxAlloy and PYPE.

rules.t: Most stringent requirement governs unless the Architect resolves it in writing first
Special Inspector is engaged by the Owner, never the Contractor
Retest and reinspection costs are charged to the Contractor
Verbal confirmation is never closure evidence

gate: QC plan submitted and followed
Deficiencies logged with party, severity, due date
NCRs closed with documented evidence

steps.title: The standards stack
steps.body: Tier 1 Owner: QTS CX Standard V1.4 (S7117) Rev 39. Tier 2 Contract: Specs 01 40 00 and 01 91 13. Tier 3 Implementation: the Suffolk Project QA/QC Plan. Tier 4 Execution: approved submittals, shop drawings and manufacturer instructions.
steps.field: When two requirements disagree, the most stringent governs unless the Architect resolves it in writing before you proceed.

steps.title: QA vs QC: layered, not shared
steps.body: The Trade Partner owns QC: self-inspection, correction and documentation of its own work. Suffolk QA verifies, tracks trends, escalates and reports. It does not perform QC for the trade. QTS witnesses Cx inspections and gives final acceptance.
steps.field: No party can delegate accountability. The Owner engages the Special Inspector under IBC Chapter 17.

steps.title: Deficiency or NCR?
steps.body: A deficiency is a documented condition that does not meet requirements, with a party, severity, due date and closure evidence. An NCR is triggered by unapproved material, damaged equipment, failed tests, concealed work, unauthorized deviations or repeat failures.
steps.field: Progress payments may be withheld for open NCRs, failed inspections, missing reports or unresolved punch items.

steps.title: Systems of record
steps.body: Procore holds RFIs, submittals, drawings, punch, observations, NCRs, EPP walks and daily reports. CxAlloy holds L1–L5 inspections, FOD events, OFCI/CFCI tracking and test reports. PYPE holds closeout and final delivery to the Owner.
steps.field: A photo on your phone is not a record. Attach it to the asset in CxAlloy or the item in Procore.

quiz.q: Two referenced standards give different torque values for the same connection. What do you do?
opts: Use the lower value to avoid over-torquing
Apply the most stringent unless the Architect resolves it in writing before you proceed
Use whichever value the foreman normally uses
quiz.why: Spec 01 40 00 §1.4: the most stringent requirement governs. Refer uncertainties to the Architect before proceeding.

modules.title: Procurement & FWT
modules.summary: Quality starts before anything ships: submittal review, an approved factory witness test plan, a documented pass, and document review before release.

role.aw: Know that major equipment is tested before it ships, and that the results follow the equipment to site.
role.pr: Attend witness tests, compare readings to the approved submittal, and log failures as CxAlloy Issues.
role.ad: Track the FWT schedule, OSI/OAI uploads, and source inspection count against the minimum of 5.

rules.t: FWT plan approved by the CxA and QTS before testing
Failed FWT steps are logged as CxAlloy Issues
Minimum 5 source inspections per project on long-lead / high-risk items
Offsite storage (OSI) and offsite arrival (OAI) uploaded within 24 hrs

gate: FWT passed and report issued
Failures resolved in CxAlloy
Mfg docs, BOL and O&M received; released to ship

steps.title: Submittal review
steps.body: DLB, the EOR and Suffolk QA/QC review submittals. The approved submittal becomes the yardstick for every later check, including the factory test.
steps.field: Bring the approved submittal to the FWT. Compare nameplates, ratings and firmware to it, not to the vendor brochure.

steps.title: FWT plan and witness
steps.body: The FWT plan names the tests and the witnesses: DLB, the vendor, QTS and Suffolk. It must be approved by the CxA and QTS. The test produces an FWT report with witnessed data.
steps.field: Skids and PODs built at an integrator also get L1 checks: offsite arrival (OAI), integration, controls FAT, vendor startup and skid testing.

steps.title: Pass, fail, ship
steps.body: A failed step becomes a CxAlloy Issue and is retested. On a pass, Suffolk QA/QC and MOFE review manufacturer docs, the bill of lading and O&M before the equipment ships.
steps.field: OFCI equipment stored offsite needs a completed Offsite Storage Inspection (L1E/M - OSI) uploaded within 24 hours.

quiz.q: A UPS fails one step of its factory witness test. Where is that recorded?
opts: As a CxAlloy Issue, tracked to resolution and retest
quiz.why: Flowchart R5: Fail → CxAlloy Issue. It stays open until resolved and retested.

modules.title: Site Acceptance & Install
modules.summary: From the truck to a sealed, verified installation. The L2 gate opens only at 100% complete with a clean walk.

role.aw: Protect installed equipment, keep FOD seals intact, and report damage the moment you see it.
role.pr: Run benchmark inspections, verify installation checklists, and call the Owner's Quality Rep for SIP and PEI.
role.ad: Track the 24-hour upload windows and the L2 gate status for every asset.

rules.t: Receipt logged in Procore RIF within 24 hours of delivery
OFCI damage or deviation reported to QTS and vendor within 48 hours
Follow-up benchmark inspections at intervals of 15 days or less
Installers complete and sign checklists daily for the prior day's work
Broken FOD seal: repeat the full FOD inspection and apply a new seal

gate: 100% of L2 checklists closed in CxAlloy
Clean walk complete, FOD seal applied and intact
Asset data (mfr, model, serial) loaded in CxAlloy

steps.title: Site arrival (SAI)
steps.body: Inspect condition on delivery: agreement with the approved submittal, cleanliness and no damage. Attach the bill of lading and applicable FAT. Required on all OFCI equipment and whenever ownership transfers.
steps.field: Log the receipt in Procore RIF within 24 hours. Damage or deviations on OFCI go to QTS and the vendor within 48 hours.

steps.title: Benchmark and set-in-place
steps.body: The first in-place installation of each type is the benchmark that sets the accepted quality. Follow-ups run at 15-day intervals or less. SIP covers first of kind plus 10%, completed by the Owner's Quality Rep.
steps.field: Non-conforming benchmark work is corrected and re-inspected before repetitive installation continues.

steps.title: Installation verification
steps.body: EIV, MIV and CIV checks confirm location, configuration, manufacturer instructions, attachment, access clearance, utilities and labeling. Electrical adds continuity, torque, cable and NETA testing, and SCCS settings.
steps.field: Installers complete and sign construction checklists daily for the preceding day's work.

steps.title: Pre-energization and clean walk
steps.body: The Owner's Quality Rep completes the PEI; the CM calls the inspection. The clean walk is the FOD inspection, and the equipment is tamper-sealed before energization.
steps.field: If a FOD seal is broken for any reason, repeat the full FOD inspection and apply a new seal. No exceptions.

quiz.q: An electrician opens a sealed switchboard to fix a missing label. What happens next?
opts: Close it and re-apply the original seal
Log a Procore observation, repeat the full FOD inspection, apply a new seal
Leave a note for the L3 startup tech
quiz.why: A broken seal triggers a Procore observation and a repeat FOD inspection with a new seal, every time.

modules.title: Startup & Pre-functional
modules.summary: Proves each piece of equipment is ready, energized safely and started per the manufacturer. Ends with CxA acceptance.
modules.leads: Suffolk Cx · DLB · CEI · Loenbro · Vendor

role.aw: Stay out of energized areas unless you are authorized. Respect every lock and tag.
role.pr: Confirm prerequisites, issue 48-hour notice, witness OEM startup, and capture the report in CxAlloy.
role.ad: Confirm every L3V and L3C checklist is marked Owner Agent Reviewed before L4 is scheduled.

rules.t: 48-hour minimum notice for any startup or dynamic operation
Prestartup audit of completed installation checks before startup
Manufacturer / factory-authorized rep field report required
Contractor test equipment calibrated and CxA-approved

gate: Startup report with as-left settings (and TAB report where applicable)
Controls (EPMS/BMS) checklist complete
CxA marks "Owner Agent Reviewed": ready for L4

steps.title: Prerequisites and prestartup audit
steps.body: Before startup, L1 and L2 are closed, the FOD seal is intact and test reports are complete. A prestartup audit reviews installation checks and reports anything that would keep the system from operating satisfactorily.
steps.field: Give at least 48 hours notice for startup or any dynamic operation.

steps.title: LOTO and initial energization
steps.body: CEI and the Suffolk MEP PM control authorization under AutoLOTO. Initial energization follows the MV to LV sequence with CEI, Loenbro, the vendor and Cx present.
steps.field: After first energization, site safety conditions change for every trade. Re-brief crews.

steps.title: Manufacturer startup
steps.body: Performed per manufacturer procedures, approved submittals and O&M documentation, with an OEM witness and field report. The startup report includes all as-left settings and an FTE check.
steps.field: The CxA marks the L3V checklist 'Owner Agent Reviewed' to show the equipment is ready for L4.

quiz.q: A chiller startup is set for Thursday 8 AM. What is the latest the notice can go out?
opts: Thursday 7 AM, if QTS is already on site
quiz.why: Startup and dynamic operations need a minimum of 48 hours notice.

modules.title: Functional Performance Test
modules.summary: DLB-owned, QTS-approved scripts test each system against design intent. Failures become CxAlloy Issues and are retested until they pass.

role.aw: System tests fail on a single missing point or label, and retests cost real money. Finish your work completely.
role.pr: Support script execution, record actual results, and log failures in CxAlloy within 24 hours.
role.ad: Track issue aging, retests and the L4 to L5 gate.

rules.t: Failed test: compliance issue report within 24 hours
One issue per report, unless a whole device class shares it
Repeat demonstrations caused by Contractor work are reimbursed to Owner
Demonstrate 100% unless ASQ Z1.4 sampling is specified

gate: All FPT scripts passed
TAB complete: air and water balance
CxA and QTS acceptance

steps.title: Scripts and TAB
steps.body: L4 scripts are owned by DLB and approved by QTS. TAB is executed by an independent AABC or NEBB-certified agency, not the mechanical contractor.
steps.field: Controls go first: point-to-point, calibration, network, alarms, trends, graphics and sequence verification.

steps.title: Testing against design intent
steps.body: Each system is tested under a full range of operating conditions and loads. Completed test data forms are the official record of results.
steps.field: Record what actually happened. Never edit an expected result to match.

steps.title: Issue, fix, retest
steps.body: Results outside acceptance criteria are compliance issues. Submit the report within 24 hours, determine the cause, correct it and retest on a new form marked "Retest".
steps.field: If every actuator in a class fails the same way, they may share one report.

quiz.q: During FPT, a CRAH alarm shows at the unit but not on the BMS. Next step?
opts: Pass it, the alarm works locally
Fail the step and submit a compliance issue report within 24 hours
quiz.why: §3.5.K.4: results outside acceptance criteria are reported within 24 hours, corrected and retested.

modules.title: MST + IST
modules.summary: Mechanical systems testing, then integrated systems testing under full load with every trade and vendor on site. Ends with QTS final acceptance.

role.aw: IST days are all-hands. Know your role in the test and where you need to be.
role.pr: Confirm readiness, coordinate trades and vendors, and support NCR resolution and re-witness.
role.ad: Maintain IST readiness tracking, NCR closure and the evidence package.

rules.t: L1–L4 fully closed in CxAlloy before L5
Scripts and load bank plan DLB-owned, QTS-approved
Vendor support mandatory; all trades on site
L5 failures route through NCR: correct, retest, re-witness

gate: MST and IST scripts passed
Failure-mode and resilience tests witnessed by QTS
IST acceptance by DLB and QTS

steps.title: MST first
steps.body: DLB, Loenbro, Baker and Cx run the Mechanical Systems Test to prove the cooling plant and controls work as systems before full integration.
steps.field: Suffolk does not author L5 scripts.

steps.title: IST at full load
steps.body: Load banks simulate IT load. Electrical, mechanical and controls run together under full load, with all trades and vendors on site.
steps.field: Vendor support is mandatory. A missing vendor can cost the IST window.

steps.title: Failure modes and resilience
steps.body: Failure scenarios are run with QTS witnessing to prove the facility rides through as designed. Failures go through the NCR workflow: corrective action, retest and re-witness.
steps.field: Successful L5 closure is the final gate to turnover under S7117 V1.4 Rev 39.

quiz.q: Can IST start while one L4 FPT is still open on a CRAH?
opts: Yes, if the CRAH isn't in the first scenario
No. L1–L4 must be fully closed first
quiz.why: L5 prerequisites: L1–L4 fully closed and commissioning readiness verified.

modules.title: Closeout & Turnover
modules.summary: Punch and clean walk, permanent systems in, temporary removed, owner training, the final Cx report, then owner acceptance.

role.aw: Close your punch items fast and completely. The 72-hour clock is real.
role.pr: Verify 'Ready for Review' punch within 48 hours and support the CxA inspection.
role.ad: Assemble closeout in PYPE: binders, PDFs and test data, plus the final Special Inspection Report.

rules.t: Punch resolution by trade partner within 72 hours
Suffolk verifies 'Ready for Review' punch within 48 hours
Final Special Inspection Report at Substantial Completion
Cx completion certificate before Substantial Completion inspection

gate: Punch and clean walk complete
Temporary cooling and power removed
Owner training, Cx final report, owner acceptance

steps.title: Punch and clean walk
steps.body: Suffolk QA/QC, Cx, the EOR and QTS walk the work. The Contractor submits a complete list of items to finish, and the CxA inspects.
steps.field: Leaving an item off the list doesn't remove the responsibility to complete it.

steps.title: Permanent systems and training
steps.body: Permanent cooling replaces temporary cooling. Temporary power is removed and verified by QA/QC. Vendors and DLB deliver owner training and burn-ins.
steps.field: Training is scheduled per §4.0 of the Cx plan.

steps.title: Final report and acceptance
steps.body: DLB issues the Cx final report with binders, PDF and test data. The CxA certificate of construction-phase Cx completion comes before the Substantial Completion inspection. QTS, DLB and Suffolk sign owner acceptance.
steps.field: Deferred checklists need written Owner approval and a completion schedule (§3.2.F).

quiz.q: Who prepares the Certificate of Construction Phase Commissioning Process Completion?
quiz.why: §3.10.D: the CxA prepares the certificate once construction-phase commissioning is complete.

modules.title: Electrical QA/QC
modules.summary: The electrical acceptance tests that stand between installation and energization.

role.aw: Know which tests must pass before gear is energized. Never work around an open test.
role.pr: Confirm NETA reports, torque and interlock verification are complete and attached before PEI.
role.ad: Track NETA, megger, TTR and grounding reports against every electrical asset.

rules.t: MV and LV switchgear field acceptance
Grounding: three-point fall-of-potential test
Transformers: TTR, winding resistance, IR, oil per ASTM D923
LV cables: insulation resistance (megger) before energization

gate: NETA acceptance reports complete
Torque, grounding and bonding verified
Kirk key / interlocks verified, labeling complete

steps.title: Switchgear and cables
steps.body: Medium- and low-voltage switchgear get NETA field acceptance testing. Low-voltage cables get insulation resistance (megger) testing before energization.
steps.field: A failed megger is a failed test: it triggers an NCR, correction and retest before energization.

steps.title: Grounding and transformers
steps.body: Grounding is tested by three-point fall-of-potential per IEEE 81. Transformer acceptance covers TTR, winding resistance, insulation resistance and oil testing per ASTM D923.
steps.field: Attach each report to the asset in CxAlloy as part of the L2 EIV.

steps.title: Energization readiness
steps.body: Torque verification, grounding and bonding, Kirk key and interlock verification, and labeling must all be complete.
steps.field: Gear, panel, transformer and UPS openings are sealed for FOD; heaters or bulbs stay on in switchboards.

quiz.q: Which method is specified for ground system testing?
quiz.why: NETA ATS §7.13 with IEEE 81: three-point fall-of-potential.

modules.title: Mechanical, Plumbing & FP
modules.summary: Test values and independent agencies for mechanical, plumbing, fire protection and concrete.

role.aw: Know the test pressures and durations so you can spot a shortcut.
role.pr: Witness hydros for the full duration, confirm certificates, and verify TAB is by an independent agency.
role.ad: Track test certificates, cylinder breaks and firestop sampling against the 10% minimum.

rules.t: TAB by an independent AABC MN-1 or NEBB agency, not the mechanical contractor
Domestic water: hydrostatic 150 psi for 4 hours; disinfect per AWWA C651
Wet sprinkler: hydrostatic 200 psi for 2 hours, with material & test certificate
Firestopping: listed UL system; destructive sample 10% minimum

gate: TAB report from an independent agency
Hydro and disinfection records with bacteriological sample
Firestop inspection and concrete test records complete

steps.title: Independent TAB
steps.body: Testing, adjusting and balancing is executed by an independent AABC MN-1 or NEBB-certified agency. It is never the mechanical contractor.
steps.field: The TAB report is attached to the system in CxAlloy before L4.

steps.title: Pressure tests
steps.body: Domestic water: hydrostatic 150 psi for 4 hours, then disinfection per AWWA C651 with a bacteriological sample. Wet sprinkler: hydrostatic 200 psi for 2 hours with the NFPA 13 contractor material and test certificate.
steps.field: A test cut short is a failed test. Restart the clock.

steps.title: Firestopping and concrete
steps.body: Firestopping is installed to the listed UL system and inspected visually and by destructive sample per ASTM E2174, 10% minimum. Concrete: cylinder breaks per ASTM C39; slump, air and temperature per ASTM C143, C231 and C1064.
steps.field: A firestop without a matching UL system is a deficiency even if it looks complete.

quiz.q: What is the wet sprinkler hydrostatic test?

modules.title: Controls / BMS / EPMS
modules.summary: Controls readiness for L3C and L4: devices, points, network, alarms, trends, graphics and sequences.

role.aw: Every point must be proven from the device to the graphic.
role.pr: Witness point-to-point, check calibration records, and confirm alarms reach the BMS/EPMS.
role.ad: Track L1C and L3C checklists and P2P completion by system.

rules.t: Every point mapped, addressed and verified (P2P)
Sensor and transmitter calibration records on file
Sequences validated against approved control drawings
L3C checklist marked Owner Agent Reviewed before L4

gate: P2P complete for every point
Network, alarms, trends and graphics validated
Sequence of operations verified

steps.title: Devices and calibration
steps.body: Devices installed and controllers labeled, with sensor and transmitter calibration records on file.
steps.field: L1C covers FAT/SFAT of BMS panels for first of kind or first in a production line.

steps.title: Point-to-point
steps.body: Every point is mapped, addressed and verified from the field device to the BMS or EPMS.
steps.field: A point that reads correctly at the controller but is mislabeled on the graphic fails P2P.

steps.title: Network, alarms and sequences
steps.body: Network verification, alarm testing, trend verification and graphics validation, then sequence of operations validation against approved control drawings. L4 FPT is logged in CxAlloy.
steps.field: The CxA marks L3C "Owner Agent Reviewed" when controls are ready for L4.

opts: Every point is mapped, addressed and verified from device to BMS/EPMS
quiz.why: P2P traces each point end to end.

items.text: Witnessing a generator load test at the manufacturer
items.why: Factory witness testing is Level 1 in Flowchart R5.

items.text: Completing the Site Arrival Inspection with the bill of lading attached
items.why: SAI (L2E/M/C - SAI) is Level 2 site acceptance.

items.text: Applying a tamper-evident FOD seal after the clean walk
items.why: The clean walk (CW) and seal close out Level 2 before energization.

items.text: OEM technician recording as-left settings on first run
Prestartup audit of completed installation checks
items.why: §3.5.E prestartup audit happens before L3 startup.

items.text: Independent agency balancing air and water flows
items.why: System TAB is part of Level 4 in Flowchart R5.

items.text: Failing a CRAH fan per DLB script and confirming the BMS alarm
items.why: Scripted system testing against design intent is Level 4 FPT.

items.text: Load banks at full load with every trade and vendor on site
Writing an NCR for unapproved material delivered to site
items.why: NCRs are a QA/QC tool that runs underneath every level.

items.text: Removing temporary power and verifying it with QA/QC
items.why: Temp power removal is a Closeout / Turnover step.

practiceSpot.q: This cable entry passed the clean walk and was sealed. An electrician now needs to pull one more cable through it. What happens?
opts: Pull the cable and push the plug back in
The seal is broken: log a Procore observation, repeat the full FOD inspection, apply a new seal
Tape around the new cable and carry on
practiceSpot.why: If a FOD seal is broken for any reason, the full FOD inspection is repeated and a new seal applied. No exceptions.

practiceSpot.q: The torque report for this joint shows a value below the approved submittal, and there is no torque mark on the bolt. Is it ready for PEI?
opts: Yes, if it is close to spec
No: log a deficiency, re-torque to spec, mark it and update the torque report before PEI
Yes, the spring washer makes up the difference
practiceSpot.why: Torque verification and the torque report are part of L2 installation verification (EIV) and energization readiness. Below spec is a deficiency.

practiceSpot.q: A pre-energization check on this transformer shows OPEN instead of O.K. What happens next?
opts: Energize it and let the vendor check it at startup
Stop: it is a failed test. Do not energize; log a deficiency/NCR, correct, retest
Re-run the test until it reads O.K.
practiceSpot.why: Failed tests trigger an NCR. Energization waits until the cause is corrected and the retest passes.

practiceSpot.q: This rooftop unit was set weeks before startup. Its intake is open, with debris on the roof and birds at the louvers. What is missing?
opts: Nothing, it will be cleaned at startup
EPP protection: cover and filter media at the intake, clean the area, log a Procore observation
practiceSpot.why: EPP mechanical scope: coverboard on top, plastic wrap, filter media at intakes. Debris in the unit becomes a FOD failure before L3 startup.

practiceSpot.q: This panel directory is handwritten, the panel name is blank, and loads read "Existing load" or "power". Is it ready for PEI?
opts: No: it needs a typed panel schedule that is complete and accurate before PEI
Yes, if the electrician knows the loads
practiceSpot.why: The project uses typed panel schedules. Correct labeling and identification is an installation check and a readiness gate item.

practiceSpot.q: This tilt indicator on an OFCI transformer crate is red at delivery. What do you do?
opts: Set the transformer; it will be tested at L3
Record it on the SAI with photos and notify QTS and the vendor within 48 hours
Peel off the indicator and continue
practiceSpot.why: OFCI damage or deviations are reported to QTS and the vendor within 48 hours, with the condition documented on the Site Arrival Inspection.

finalExam.q: During an EPP walk you find a FOD seal on a UPS broken. What is required?
opts: Re-tape the seal and note it
Procore observation, repeat the full FOD inspection, apply a new seal

finalExam.q: A feeder fails its megger test the day before energization. What happens?
opts: Stop: document the failed test as a deficiency/NCR, correct, retest before energization

finalExam.q: The spec and a referenced standard conflict on a test value. You…
opts: Apply the most stringent unless the Architect resolves it in writing first

finalExam.q: Unapproved material arrives on site. This triggers…
OFCI equipment arrives damaged. Notify QTS and the vendor within…
Equipment receipt must be logged in Procore RIF within…
Minimum notice for a startup or dynamic operation is…
Follow-up benchmark inspections occur at intervals no greater than…
Does Suffolk QA perform QC for the trade partner?
opts: No. Suffolk verifies; the trade owns its QC

finalExam.q: Where are L1–L5 inspections and FOD events recorded?
A test demonstration fails. The compliance issue report is due within…
Can L5 IST begin with an L4 item still open?
opts: No. L1–L4 must be fully closed

finalExam.q: A foreman says a deficiency is fixed. Can you close it?
opts: No. Closure needs evidence: reinspection, photos or updated report

finalExam.q: Trade partners must resolve punch items within…

glossary.name: QTS CX Standard V1.4 Rev 39
glossary.def: The Owner commissioning standard (10/23/2025). Tier 1 of the standards stack.

glossary.name: Commissioning Authority
glossary.def: DLB on the CDR Campus. Owns L4/L5 scripts and issues the Cx completion certificate.

glossary.name: CxA + 3rd-party QA/QC
glossary.def: The commissioning authority and third-party QA/QC firm.

glossary.name: Owner Furnished, Contractor Installed
glossary.def: Equipment bought by QTS and installed by the contractor.

glossary.name: Contractor Furnished, Contractor Installed
glossary.def: Equipment bought and installed by the contractor.

glossary.name: Factory Witness Test
glossary.def: Level 1 test at the manufacturer, witnessed per an approved plan. Also FAT.

glossary.name: Offsite Storage / Offsite Arrival Inspection
glossary.def: L1 checklists for equipment stored offsite or received at an integrator.

glossary.name: Site Arrival Inspection
glossary.def: L2 receipt inspection with BOL and FAT attached.

glossary.name: Set-in-Place Inspection
glossary.def: L2Q check by the Owner's Quality Rep; first of kind + 10%.

glossary.name: Electrical / Mechanical / Controls Installation Verification
glossary.def: L2 checks that installed equipment meets the specs.

glossary.name: Vendor Pre-Startup
glossary.def: L2V vendor forms confirming readiness for L3.

glossary.name: Pre-Energization Inspection
glossary.def: L2Q check by the Owner's Quality Rep before energization.

glossary.name: Clean Walk
glossary.def: L2 FOD inspection followed by the tamper seal.

glossary.name: Foreign Object & Debris
glossary.def: Inspection and tamper-evident seal before energization or startup.

glossary.name: Equipment Protection Plan
glossary.def: Protection program with Suffolk walks at least twice daily.

glossary.name: Non-Conformance Report
glossary.def: Raised for unapproved material, damage, failed tests, concealed work, deviations or repeat failures.

glossary.name: Functional Performance Test
glossary.def: Level 4 scripted test of a system against design intent.

glossary.name: Testing, Adjusting & Balancing
glossary.def: Air and water balance by an independent AABC or NEBB agency.

glossary.name: Mechanical Systems Test
glossary.def: Level 5 test of the mechanical systems ahead of IST.

glossary.name: Integrated Systems Test
glossary.def: Level 5 full-load test of all systems together.

glossary.name: NETA Acceptance Testing Spec
glossary.def: Field acceptance testing standard for electrical equipment.

glossary.name: Engineer of Record
glossary.def: The design engineer responsible for the work.
